subject: ESCALATED: the whole Docker VM is down, not just mcp-server. Engine self-shutdown at 05:47:38Z after 'service fs failed: injecting event blocked for 60s'. NOT the 2026-07-15 hypervisor class. Needs host action.

ESCALATION.what_changed: At the 05:45Z tick the preflight error text changed from the session-init message to 'transport failure calling https://zenmidi.com/vn-market'. That was not noise — it was the SECOND URL dying too. docker ps now returns nothing: 'Docker Desktop is unable to start'. All 13 containers are down, not just mcp-server.
ESCALATION.scope: frontend, pdf-extractor, mcp-server, alert-engine, rag-service, news-fetch, api-gateway, stock-price, macro-indicators, mcp-gateway, flaresolverr, technical-analysis, kinh-dich-service.
ESCALATION.why_URL2_also_failed: mcp-gateway is itself a container. It went down with the VM. That is why the failover URL flipped from answering-with-an-error to not answering at all.

ROOT_CAUSE_from_the_backend_log.reading: A 60-second watchdog on Docker's host<->VM file-sharing service fired and the engine shut ITSELF down. This was an orderly self-shutdown triggered by an fs-layer stall, not a crash.
ROOT_CAUSE_from_the_backend_log.current_state: Docker Desktop is running a GUI process '--name=error-dialog' (PID 2974, up 4m46s) — an error dialog is on screen awaiting a human.

THIS_IS_NOT_THE_2026_07_15_HYPERVISOR_CL.why_it_matters: feedback_docker_hypervisor_crash_cli_recovery_exhausted_user_only says CLI recovery is exhausted and user-only for THAT signature. Applying it here without checking would be cargo-culting a conclusion from a different failure.
THIS_IS_NOT_THE_2026_07_15_HYPERVISOR_CL.discriminator_2_hypervisor_error: 2026-07-15: hypervisor.error.json showed 'Internal Virtualization error, VM stopped unexpectedly'. Now: that file DOES NOT EXIST anywhere under the Docker Data dir.
THIS_IS_NOT_THE_2026_07_15_HYPERVISOR_CL.discriminator_3_backend: 2026-07-15: backend respawned but socket never bootstrapped. Now: backend is alive and answering IPC; it is the ENGINE that stopped, by its own request.
THIS_IS_NOT_THE_2026_07_15_HYPERVISOR_CL.conclusion: Different class. The engine performed a clean self-shutdown after an fs watchdog. Do NOT declare CLI recovery exhausted on the strength of the July incident — that ladder was climbed against a different fault.

THE_LINK_TO_THE_0516Z_HANG_IS_NOT_ESTABL.temptation: mcp-server hung at 05:16:16Z with a write-visibility error, and the VM's fs service wedged later. It is very tempting to call these one fault.
THE_LINK_TO_THE_0516Z_HANG_IS_NOT_ESTABL.why_I_am_NOT_claiming_that: They are 30 minutes apart, and the Docker API was demonstrably HEALTHY in between — container event streams were serving normally right up to 05:46:37Z. A single fs-layer fault that had already blocked mcp-server at 05:16 should not have left the engine healthy for the next half hour.
THE_LINK_TO_THE_0516Z_HANG_IS_NOT_ESTABL.what_is_fair_to_say: Both are filesystem/IO-layer symptoms and a shared root cause is a live hypothesis worth testing. It is NOT established, and must not be written into a remedy.
THE_LINK_TO_THE_0516Z_HANG_IS_NOT_ESTABL.correction_to_my_own_earlier_filing: In cowork-team-20260825T052633Z I called the 05:16Z hang a 'DEADLOCK / blocked event loop' — which implied an mcp-server APPLICATION bug and an mcp-server owner. That attribution is now unsafe: an equally consistent explanation is that the container was blocked on host-side IO. The observations (CPU 0.13%, flat memory, silent-on-a-write) fit both. Do not assign that row to a dev-* zone on the strength of my earlier wording.

RECOVERY_and_the_TRAP.likely_sufficient: Quit Docker Desktop fully and relaunch it (the error dialog on screen may itself offer Restart). This is a stopped engine, not a faulted hypervisor.
RECOVERY_and_the_TRAP.THE_TRAP_do_not_do_this: Do NOT 'rebuild the VM from scratch' by removing ~/Library/Containers/com.docker.docker/Data/vms. On Docker Desktop/Mac, named volumes live INSIDE the VM disk image, so that step DESTROYS market_data and bctc-page-images. It happened on 2026-07-15 and required restoring a 361MB backup. Host bind-mounts (./docs/data, ./data/pdfs) survive; named volumes do not.
RECOVERY_and_the_TRAP.if_it_does_come_back: Verify volume integrity BEFORE trusting green health — row counts and MAX(date) on market.db. Green health on an empty DB masks total data loss (feedback_vm_rebuild_destroys_named_volumes_restore_then_launch).
RECOVERY_and_the_TRAP.not_a_disk_problem: Checked: host / has 28Gi free, Docker.raw is 20G actual (233G is only the sparse apparent size). Host swap is tight (5312/6144M used) — noted, not diagnosed as the cause.
